How to edit your custom CSS stylesheet within the page itself

Note: Voat’s new CSS editor includes a live preview function. Go to your subverse and select “edit stylesheet” in the bottom of the sidebar. I still prefer my bookmarklet as it works instantly without having to send/receive data.

Updated 2015-08-03: The bookmarklet now works on comment pages! It checks for and removes the duplicate #custom_css element to prevent errors.

Setup

Add a blank bookmark to your browser’s bookmarks bar, and replace the URL with this. Make sure to copy the entire line, with no extra linebreaks:

javascript:(function(){var r=document.querySelector("body > #custom_css"),s=document.querySelector("#container > #custom_css");s.classList.contains("j_livecss")?s.style.display="none"===s.style.display?"block":"none":(null!==r&&null!==s&&r.parentNode.removeChild(r),s.setAttribute("style","display:block;position:fixed;bottom:0;left:0;height:400px;max-width:800px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.9);color:#000;opacity:.5;font:10px/1.1 monospace;white-space:pre;overflow:scroll;-webkit-user-modify:read-write-plaintext-only;"),s.classList.add("j_livecss"),s.setAttribute("contentEditable",!0),s.setAttribute("onfocus","this.style.opacity=1"),s.setAttribute("onblur","this.style.opacity=.5"),s.focus())})()

Usage

  1. Click the bookmarklet once to enable the overlay. Click again to toggle its display.

  2. Any changes made to the CSS rules in the overlay will be reflected live on the page.

  3. When you are done editing, copy the contents of the overlay, and paste it into the custom CSS box in your subverse’s settings page.

Note: your changes are live on your screen only, and are not saved! Don't leave the page until you copy the code.

You can also use this bookmarklet on other subverses to easily view their custom stylesheet.

Reference

This is the un-minified source. You can change the style of the overlay if you need it bigger/smaller/a different colour/whatever, then run it through a JavaScript optimiser like Closure Compiler or UglifyJS to use as a bookmarklet.

javascript:(function () {
 var r = document.querySelector("body > #custom_css"),
 s = document.querySelector("#container > #custom_css");
 if (s.classList.contains("j_livecss")) {
 s.style.display = s.style.display === "none" ? "block" : "none";
 } else {
 if (r !== null && s !== null) {
 r.parentNode.removeChild(r);
 }
 s.setAttribute("style", "display:block;position:fixed;bottom:0;left:0;height:400px;max-width:800px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.9);color:#000;opacity:.5;font:10px/1.1 monospace;white-space:pre;overflow:scroll;-webkit-user-modify:read-write-plaintext-only;");
 s.classList.add("j_livecss");
 s.setAttribute("contentEditable", true);
 s.setAttribute("onfocus", "this.style.opacity=1");
 s.setAttribute("onblur", "this.style.opacity=.5");
 s.focus();
 }
})()

This trick makes use of two properties:

  • the CSS rule -webkit-user-modify: read-write-plaintext-only;
  • and the HTML attribute contentEditable

to turn the <style> element into an editable textarea on most browsers.

Tested with Chrome 42/43, Firefox, and Safari on OS X, and Chrome 43 on Windows.
